Vacillate

VAS-uh-layt · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To vacillate to be indecisive, wavering repeatedly between different opinions or actions.

The board vacillated for months over the merger, approving it one week and shelving it the next.

Worked Example

The senator vacillated publicly on the bill, voting for an early draft, then against a later one, then sitting out the final vote entirely.

Vacillate describes repeated wavering on something significant, not a single quick change of mind.

How Strong Is It? — hesitate → flip-flop → vacillate

hesitate vs. vacillate

hesitate vs. vacillate: Anyone might hesitate for a second before answering a hard question.

flip-flop vs. vacillate

flip-flop vs. vacillate: A politician who flip-flops constantly can end up trusted by no one at all.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — vacill-

root — vacill-: to sway, stagger, totter (Latin vacillare)

suffix — -ate

suffix — -ate: to make or perform an action (Latin -atus)

Put it together

Put it together: Vacillate comes from Latin vacillare, "to sway or totter," as if the person's mind were physically staggering back and forth between two positions.

Use the root in a new word: vacillation

Use the root in a new word: vacillation: His constant vacillation between two career paths left his parents unsure what to write on the graduation announcement.

Word Choice

Vacillate works best for a real, repeated back-and-forth on something that matters -- a policy, a major decision -- not a single quick change of heart.
